BUILDPLAN.md T-23 (M4).

**Guardrail audit** — an adversarial read of all merged code against G-1…G-12 and the phase invariants; files gap tickets

Criteria: G-1…G-12
Harness hooks: see EVALUATION.md rows for those IDs; `just test` is the inner loop (≤ 60 s).
Depends on (BUILDPLAN): everything above
BUILDPLAN notes: The Phase-4 pass, re-run on the built tree

Orchestrator notes: Runs last, on the assembled tree. Files gap tickets; does not fix.

Workflow mode: sub-agent-full. Terminal pre-merge status: review. PR base: origin/main.
Standing clauses: criteria outrank SPEC on behaviour, state, payloads and copy; SPEC outranks the prototype, which wins on visual detail only. Never write down what a program prints. Answer position is a uniform draw from the date, never balanced. Miri proves absence of UB on executed paths only. Colour is never the only signal. Code never causes horizontal page scroll. Never `git add -A`. Signing goes through 1Password: retry once, then escalate.

Plan: filled in by the delegator's plan phase.

CONTRACT NOTE PQ-28 (1/3) SPEC §3.2 / G-2: nothing binds a verified record to the run that produced it. A hand edit that keeps a record self-consistent (verified.stdout and the matching option text changed together) passes check_provenance (verify.py:592-596 says so); the only catch is test_migration's replay, which covers the fixed tuple MIGRATED = (q3,q4,q7,q8) (migrate_mvp.py:76), so a fifth question has none. Closing it needs a field the contract lacks (a digest over the record, or the recording id). Audit GAP-6.

CONTRACT NOTE PQ-28 (2/3) G-11 vs AC-25: SPEC G-11 says 'organizer docs carry the tells'; EVALUATION AC-25 says the lint runs over 'the organizer docs'. The code scans mvp/PRACTICE-RUN.md and mvp/FIELD-NOTES-TEMPLATE.md (organizer docs) but not docs/RUNBOOK.md (audit.py:636-647). The contract should say which organizer docs may carry tells. Audit GAP-22.

CONTRACT NOTE PQ-28 (3/3) G-12 / SPEC §3.1 review: affirmation records who and when but not what. Nothing ties affirmed_by/affirmed_at to the explains, why_tempting and trace text that was affirmed, and review.status 'edited' does not clear it, so text edited after affirmation schedules as affirmed. T-18 (PQ-23) will need the rule. Audit GAP-24.

ORCHESTRATOR NOTE (lead, verify it yourself before it enters the report): run directly, the standalone fallback builder puts the answer at E for every committed question. Checked from this seat on 0c7d60a: all four records (q3 q4 q7 q8) store the correct option at index 4 = E. fallback.py:27-29 renders options 'in the order they are given' and leaves arranging to the caller. main() (fallback.py:306-334) loads the record and calls write_fallback with no arrange step. 'python -m popquiz.fallback q3 --bake' ran from this seat with exit 0 and baked option E = '[1, 2, 3, 2, 1]', q3's answer. Only schedule.py:529-533 arranges by date before building the fallback. room/README.md:596 documents the standalone form; docs/RUNBOOK.md points organizers at just schedule. Report it under G-1 as you find it. Your severity call (ruling 6) — consider that the fallback is what gets projected when the wifi fails, so a standalone build would show E at every meetup. No test catches it as far as I can see. Cross-reference PQ-48 (stored order) and say whether this is new.
